title: Hybrid dataclass↔pydantic streaming adapters and idempotent-retry semantics
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Goal: Provide a lightweight, production-safe adapter layer that lets SDK consumers declare structured response types as dataclasses for minimal runtime overhead, optionally validate fields with Pydantic on-demand, and receive partial, checkpointed objects during streaming responses. This ticket implements the adapter API, streaming hydration checkpoints, and idempotent retry tokens so clients can safely reattempt failed streams without duplication or state corruption. Motivation: many users want the ergonomics and low-cost memory profile of dataclasses, but need the strict validation and helpful error messages Pydantic offers for a subset of fields. Combining both in an opt-in, incremental validation path reduces CPU and latency overhead while keeping safety for critical fields.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce Adapter API: from_dataclass(cls) and from_pydantic(cls, validate_on='final'|'field'|'none') factory hooks
Streaming parser emits partially-hydrated dataclass instances at configurable checkpoints (default every 512 tokens)
Retries use idempotency-token header and stream checkpoint cursor so a resumed call continues from last confirmed checkpoint without duplicate application-level events
Memory profile of dataclass-only path is <= 60% of equivalent full-pydantic path in benchmark harness for typical assistant responses (~1.2k tokens)
Example cookbook and notebook demonstrating: (a) low-overhead dataclass-only usage, (b) hybrid dataclass+Pydantic validation, (c) resuming an interrupted stream with idempotent retries
Unit tests covering: partial hydration, schema evolution (added optional fields), retry resume semantics, and backpressure scenarios

Implementation: streaming parser changes and checkpoint emitter (owner: Priya Rao)
Retry protocol: idempotency + cursor semantics and client retry coordinator (owner: Ben Lewis)

Design review and security review sign-off if necessary (owner: Marco)
design_decisions: Checkpoint interval default = 512 tokens to balance latency and recovery granularity
Adapter returns lightweight wrapper implementing Mapping protocol for zero-copy access during partial hydration
Validation modes: 'none' (fastest), 'final' (validate only when stream completes), 'field' (eager validate each field as it arrives) — default 'final'
Retry resume embeds last-accepted-checkpoint-id in idempotency header; server fast-forwards token cursor and streams next events
We do not attempt to reconcile conflicting edits across resumed streams; consumers responsible for idempotent handlers or deterministic apply semantics
Expose a small public helper: safe_resume(retry_token, last_checkpoint_id) so app code isn't dealing with low-level headers
progress_updates: 2025-10-06 - Ayesha: RFC posted in #sdk-python and confluence: Hybrid adapters and checkpointed streaming (link below). Seeking design feedback.
2025-10-08 - Marco: Completed API sketch and sample code for review. Opted for simple Mapping wrapper over partial dataclass to keep attribute access ergonomic.
2025-10-10 - Priya: Implemented streaming checkpoint emitter and basic partial-hydration logic. Added metrics for checkpoint latency and memory usage.
2025-10-13 - Sefa: Ran initial benchmarks; dataclass-only path shows 2.1x lower peak memory vs full-pydantic for 1k token responses. Need more CI runs for variance stabilisation.

2025-10-16 - Ben: Prototype retry header semantics implemented; verified server resume logic in local runtime against simulated disconnects. Edge case: duplicate finalizer event observed when client reconnected before ACKing last checkpoint, added dedupe token on client-side apply.
2025-10-20 - QA: Integration tests added for resume flow and schema evolution; two failing tests remain around optional enum deserialization during partial hydration (investigating)

Blocking note: Concurrency/async finalization ordering causes rare KeyError when mixed with user-supplied __post_init__ that mutates nested lists. Mitigation: document and add guard in adapter to snapshot lists into tuples during partial hydration.
review_feedback: PM review (Rita): Emphasize migration path for existing users who rely on Pydantic validation for security-sensitive fields; propose default 'final' validation to avoid breaking behavior
Design review (Evan): Prefer keeping adapter surface minimal; avoid exposing internal checkpoint objects directly — added safe_resume helper and Mapping wrapper
Security (Jules): Ensure idempotency token cannot be forged; recommend rotation and TTL enforcement on server side. Called out adding audit log entry on resume events
Performance (Nora): Add microbench fixture to CI that runs on representative input sizes to detect regressions early
testing_plan: Unit tests for adapter factories and Mapping wrapper behavior
Fuzz tests for partial hydration ordering and schema evolution (missing/extra fields)
Integration test that simulates network disconnects at random token boundaries and asserts no duplicate application-level events after resume
Performance CI that compares memory/CPU per-token against baseline every PR touching adapter code
notes: Migration guidance: existing users of pydantic.BaseModel should be able to switch to dataclass path by replacing model class and passing validate_on='final' for feature parity
Future work: Explore optional C-extension for zero-copy field binding for extreme memory-constrained environments
Related tickets: consider follow-up to provide TypeScript equivalents for browser SDK streaming ergonomics
